podcast.title: Planned Collaboration (1958)
podcast.body: Buddy Holly had ambitious plans to record an album of gospel duets with Mahalia Jackson, part of his creative explosion after leaving Norman Petty. "An album of duets on gospel songs with Mahalia Jackson."

podcast.title: Chicago Presence (1940s)
podcast.body: Mahalia Jackson was living and performing in Chicago during Sam Cooke's formative years in the 1940s, contributing to the city's vibrant gospel scene. "Dorsey, Mahalia Jackson and Sister Rosetta Tharp were all living and performing in the city during Young Sam's formative years"

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty: "You Send Me" by Sam Cooke

podcast.title: Family Friend and Caretaker
podcast.body: Mahalia Jackson, a gospel legend, was a family friend who lived near the Franklin's home in Detroit. She played a role in raising Aretha Franklin and her four siblings after their mother's death and their father's frequent travels, ensuring Aretha was surrounded by vocal legends during her turbulent childhood. "Including no kidding, gospel legend, Mahalia Jackson, a family friend who lived near the Franklin's home in Detroit."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: Say a Little Prayer Edition Part 1

podcast.title: Part of Chicago Gospel Scene
podcast.body: Mahalia Jackson was a central figure in the Chicago gospel scene, known for performing church music for church people. Sister Rosetta Tharp, although living in Chicago at the same time, was not generally considered part of this specific scene due to her traveling and performing for diverse audiences. "While she lived in Chicago at the same time as Thomas Dorsey and Mahalia Jackson, she isn't generally considered part of the gospel scene that they were at the centre of, because she was travelling around the country playing at revival meetings rather than staying in one place."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
